title: nuclear refactor: adopt lalph effect patterns & architecture
description:
Comprehensive refactor of the plot orchestrator to adopt modern Effect-TS patterns and architecture from [lalph](https://github.com/tim-smart/lalph) by tim smart (core effect-ts maintainer).

## motivation

lalph solves the same problem as plot (LLM agent orchestration driven by issue trackers) but uses bleeding-edge effect patterns that are more ergonomic, reactive, and resilient. since plot is pre-production, we can break API freely to achieve better architecture.

## scope

### effect patterns
- migrate services to `ServiceMap.Service` (from `Effect.Service` / `Context.Tag`)
- adopt `Effect.fnUntraced` as standard function wrapper
- introduce `Reactivity` + `Atom` + `AtomRegistry` for reactive state (replace manual polling/SubscriptionRef)
- use `ScopedRef` for hot-swappable service instances (tracker client resilience)
- use `RcMap` for resource-counted API clients
- add `PersistedCache` / `Persistable` for durable caching with schema validation

### architecture
- enrich the tracker plugin trait (richer IssueSource with preset routing, state enforcement, auto-merge labels)
- extract GitFlow as a strategy pattern (PR flow vs commit flow as swappable Layers)
- add stall detection (no-output timeout kills hung agents)
- add task timeout → auto-decomposition (failures become progress)
- add github etag caching (API rate-limit relief)
- add model routing by issue label
- add merge conflict recovery (auto-retry with context)
- add live task steer via stream (push task updates to running agents)
- add research agent phase (pre-implementation codebase research)

## reference
- source repo: https://github.com/tim-smart/lalph
- author: tim smart (effect-ts core maintainer)
- key files: src/Github.ts, src/IssueSource.ts, src/GitFlow.ts, src/Workers.ts, src/Prd.ts, src/Worktree.ts, src/CurrentIssueSource.ts, src/PromptGen.ts, src/commands/root.ts

## non-goals
- CLI prompt-based configuration (we have web/tui)
- yaml-based PRD file sync (we have workpad comments)
- clanka integration (tim's specific tool)
- single-package architecture (our monorepo is better for extensibility)

title: add task timeout → auto-decomposition
description:
When an agent times out on a task, instead of just failing, spawn a new agent that researches why it took too long and breaks the task into smaller sub-tasks.

## what changes

### packages/plot/src/core/application/dispatch.ts
- on timeout, instead of marking failed, run a decomposition agent
- decomposition agent: research codebase, mark original done, create smaller tasks with deps

### packages/plot/src/agent/
- add decomposition agent prompt template
- agent gets: original task, timeout context, instructions to break down

## pattern (from lalph)

```typescript
// timeout handler prompt
const promptTimeout = (options) =>
  `Your earlier attempt to complete task ${options.taskId} took too long.
  1. Investigate why the task took too long
  2. Mark the original task as "done"
  3. Break down into smaller tasks
  4. Setup task dependencies
  5. If specs need updating, update them`

// in the run loop
Effect.timeout(options.runTimeout),
Effect.tapErrorTag("TimeoutError", () =>
  agentTimeout({ task, stallTimeout, preset })
),
```

## reference
- lalph: src/Agents/timeout.ts
- lalph: src/commands/root.ts (timeout handling in run function)
- lalph: src/PromptGen.ts (promptTimeout, promptTimeoutClanka)
- repo: https://github.com/tim-smart/lalph

## verification
- `bun run typecheck` passes
- timed-out tasks produce smaller sub-tasks instead of permanent failure
- original task is marked appropriately

title: add merge conflict recovery
description:
When a merge/rebase fails due to conflicts, instead of permanent failure, prepend context to the task description and reset to todo for retry.

## what changes

### packages/plot/src/core/application/dispatch.ts
- catch merge conflict errors in post-work phase
- prepend merge conflict instruction to task description
- reset task state to allow retry

### packages/plot/src/core/git-flow-pr.ts and git-flow-commit.ts
- detect rebase/merge failures
- call flagUnmergable helper

## pattern (from lalph)

```typescript
const mergeConflictInstruction =
  "A previous attempt at this task resulted in merge conflicts. " +
  "Please try implementing the task again."

const flagUnmergable = Effect.fnUntraced(function* (options) {
  const issue = current.find(entry => entry.id === options.issueId)
  if (!issue) return
  const hasInstruction = issue.description.includes(mergeConflictInstruction)
  const nextDescription = hasInstruction
    ? issue.description
    : mergeConflictInstruction + "\n\n---\n\n" + issue.description.trim()
  yield* source.updateIssue({
    issueId: issue.id,
    description: nextDescription,
    state: "todo",
  })
})
```

## reference
- lalph: src/Prd.ts (flagUnmergable, mergeConflictInstruction)
- lalph: src/GitFlow.ts (postWork error handling in GitFlowCommit)
- repo: https://github.com/tim-smart/lalph

## verification
- `bun run typecheck` passes
- merge conflicts reset task with context instead of permanent failure
- retry run gets merge conflict context in task description

title: add live task steer via stream
description:
When a user edits a task description while an agent is running, push the updated description to the running agent as a steering message.

## what changes

### packages/plot/src/core/application/dispatch.ts
- watch for task description changes while agent is running
- debounce changes (10s)
- push updates to agent via steering stream

### packages/plot/src/agent/
- agent runner accepts optional steer stream
- steering messages are injected as additional context to the running agent

## pattern (from lalph)

```typescript
const taskUpdateSteer = Effect.fnUntraced(function* (options) {
  const registry = yield* AtomRegistry.AtomRegistry
  return AtomRegistry.toStreamResult(registry, currentIssuesAtom(projectId)).pipe(
    Stream.drop(1),
    Stream.debounce(Duration.seconds(10)),
    Stream.filterMap((issues) => {
      const issue = issues.find(entry => entry.id === options.issueId)
      if (!issue || !issue.isChangedComparedTo(options.current.current)) return Result.failVoid
      return Result.succeed(`The task has been updated. Here is the latest:
# ${issue.title}
${issue.description}`)
    }),
  )
})
```

## reference
- lalph: src/commands/root.ts (taskUpdateSteer function)
- repo: https://github.com/tim-smart/lalph

## verification
- `bun run typecheck` passes
- editing task while agent runs pushes update to agent
- agent acknowledges updated context

  Do not make any code changes.
  Include: key file names, line numbers, code snippets, key discoveries.`

title: steal GithubCli effect service for structured PR feedback extraction
description:
Port lalph's `GithubCli` service (and supporting domain models) into the plot codebase. This service provides structured PR feedback extraction via graphql, bot comment filtering, and auto-detection of owner/repo.

## what to steal (verbatim, then adapt)

### src/Github/Cli.ts
`GithubCli` service using `ServiceMap.Service`:
- auto-detects `owner`/`repo` from `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`
- `reviewComments(pr)` — graphql query fetching review comments, review threads, general comments
- `prFeedbackMd(pr)` — renders all PR feedback as structured XML markdown for agent consumption
- bot comment filtering (dependabot, renovate, coderabbit, etc.)
- review thread awareness (skips collapsed/resolved threads)
- diff hunk context in review comments

### src/domain/GithubComment.ts
Schema-validated domain models:
- `Author`, `Comment` (with `isBot` getter), `ReviewComment`
- `PullRequest`, `PullRequestComments`, `ReviewThreads`, `ReviewThreadsNode`
- `GithubPullRequestData` (top-level graphql response)

### src/Github/TokenManager.ts
OAuth device flow token management:
- persistent token storage via `KeyValueStore`
- semaphore-gated lazy auth
- device code flow polling with backoff

## where it goes in plot

### packages/plot/src/tracker/github/
- `cli.ts` — GithubCli service (adapted to plot conventions)
- `token-manager.ts` — TokenManager service
- `domain/github-comment.ts` — domain models

### integration points
- used by rework flow to extract PR feedback for the agent
- used by `plot-land` skill for review sweep
- replaces any ad-hoc `gh pr view` calls with structured graphql queries

## graphql query (steal verbatim)

```graphql
query FetchPRComments($owner: String!, $repo: String!, $pr: Int!) {
  repository(owner: $owner, name: $repo) {
    pullRequest(number: $pr) {
      url
      reviewDecision
      reviews(first: 100) {
        nodes { id, author { login }, body }
      }
      reviewThreads(first: 100) {
        nodes {
          isCollapsed, isResolved
          comments(first: 100) {
            nodes { id, author { login }, body, path, originalLine, diffHunk, createdAt }
          }
        }
      }
      comments(first: 100) {
        nodes { id, body, author { login }, createdAt }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## key patterns
- `ServiceMap.Service` with static `.layer`
- `ChildProcess` + `ChildProcessSpawner` for `gh` CLI invocation (adapt to `@effect/platform` `Command`)
- `Schema.fromJsonString` for graphql response decoding
- XML rendering for agent-consumable PR feedback

## reference
- lalph: src/Github/Cli.ts (full service)
- lalph: src/Github/TokenManager.ts (oauth device flow)
- lalph: src/domain/GithubComment.ts (domain models)
- repo: https://github.com/tim-smart/lalph

## verification
- `bun run typecheck` passes
- graphql query returns structured PR feedback
- bot comments are filtered out
- resolved/collapsed review threads are skipped
- feedback markdown renders correctly for agent consumption

title: migrate CLI from @effect/cli to effect/unstable/cli
description:
Migrate plot's CLI from the stable `@effect/cli` package to the new `effect/unstable/cli` API that ships inside the effect monorepo.

## why

- `effect/unstable/cli` is where effect is heading — the stable `@effect/cli` will be deprecated
- unlocks `Flag.withFallbackConfig(Config.*)` for env var fallback (eliminates manual `process.env` reads)
- `Command.provide(layer)` enables per-command DI (load only what each command needs)
- `Command.withSharedFlags` deduplicates cross-cutting options
- `Command.make("name", { flags })` + `Command.withHandler(...)` is more composable than 3-arg form
- enables future interactive prompts via `Prompt.*` for local dev workflows

## what changes

### packages/plot/src/cli/index.ts
- replace `import { Command, HelpDoc } from "@effect/cli"` with `import { Command, Flag } from "effect/unstable/cli"`
- replace `BunContext.layer` with `NodeRuntime.runMain` (or keep bun via platform-bun equivalent)
- use `Command.run({ version })` pipe style
- add `Layer.CurrentMemoMap` for global singleton layers (lalph pattern)

### packages/plot/src/cli/shared/options.ts
- replace `Options.boolean`, `Options.text`, `Options.integer`, `Options.choice` with `Flag.*` equivalents
- use `Flag.withFallbackConfig(Config.string("PLOT_WORKFLOW"))` instead of manual env reads
- use `Flag.withDefault(...)` for defaults
- convert to shared flags object for `Command.withSharedFlags`

### packages/plot/src/cli/commands/serve.ts
- `Command.make("serve", { flags })` + `Command.withHandler(...)` style
- `Command.provide(layer)` for service injection

### packages/plot/src/cli/commands/tui.ts
- same pattern migration

### packages/plot/src/cli/commands/web.ts
- same pattern migration

### packages/plot/src/cli/commands/auth.ts
- replace `Args.choice` with `Command.withSubcommands` (status/login/logout as subcommands instead of args)
- or keep as args with new API equivalent

### packages/plot/src/cli/commands/login.ts, logout.ts
- adapt to new API

### packages/plot/package.json
- remove `@effect/cli` dependency (it's now built into effect)

## API migration cheatsheet

```typescript
// BEFORE (@effect/cli)
import { Command, Options, Args } from "@effect/cli"

const opts = {
  port: Options.integer("port").pipe(Options.withDefault(3000)),
  verbose: Options.boolean("verbose"),
}
const cmd = Command.make("serve", opts, (args) => Effect.gen(function* () { ... }))

// AFTER (effect/unstable/cli)
import { Command, Flag } from "effect/unstable/cli"

const port = Flag.integer("port").pipe(Flag.withDefault(3000))
const verbose = Flag.boolean("verbose").pipe(Flag.withAlias("v"))

const cmd = Command.make("serve", { port, verbose }).pipe(
  Command.withHandler(
    Effect.fnUntraced(function* ({ port, verbose }) { ... })
  ),
  Command.provide(SomeLayer),
)
```

## global singleton pattern (steal from lalph)

```typescript
// shared/runtime.ts
import { Layer } from "effect"
import { Atom } from "effect/unstable/reactivity"

export const plotMemoMap = Layer.makeMemoMapUnsafe()
export const atomRuntime = Atom.context({ memoMap: plotMemoMap })

// cli/index.ts
cmd.pipe(
  Command.run({ version }),
  Effect.provideService(Layer.CurrentMemoMap, plotMemoMap),
  NodeRuntime.runMain,
)
```

## reference
- lalph: src/cli.ts (root CLI wiring with Command.provide, Layer.CurrentMemoMap)
- lalph: src/commands/root.ts (Flag.*, Command.withSharedFlags, Command.withHandler)
- lalph: src/commands/plan.ts (Command.withSubcommands, Flag.file, Flag.boolean with aliases)
- lalph: src/shared/runtime.ts (atomRuntime + memoMap singleton)
- repo: https://github.com/tim-smart/lalph

## verification
- `bun run typecheck` passes
- `bun run lint` passes
- `bun run test` passes
- all CLI commands work: `plot-ai`, `plot-ai serve`, `plot-ai web`, `plot-ai auth *`
- `--help` output renders correctly for all commands
- env var fallbacks work (PLOT_WORKFLOW, PLOT_PORT, etc.)
- `@effect/cli` removed from package.json dependencies

title: upgrade effect to v4 beta (prerequisite for all unstable/* APIs)

title: adopt Effect.fnUntraced as standard function wrapper
introduce Reactivity + Atom for orchestrator state
description:
Replace manual polling (`pollLoop` + `requestTick`) and `SubscriptionRef` in the orchestrator with `Reactivity`, `Atom`, and `AtomRegistry` from effect.

## what changes

### packages/plot/src/core/orchestrator.ts
- replace `SubscriptionRef.make<OrchestratorState>` with `Atom.make`
- replace `SubscriptionRef.make<ResolvedConfig>` with `Atom.make`
- use `AtomRegistry` for mounting/unmounting atoms
- use `Reactivity.mutation` to invalidate caches on writes (tracker writes, config changes)
- replace `PubSub` for events with `Atom` + streaming

### packages/plot/src/core/application/
- dispatch.ts and reconcile.ts: adapt to atom-based state
- orchestrator-state.ts: keep the domain logic, change how it is stored

### packages/plot/src/tracker/
- tracker client operations that write should be wrapped with `reactivity.mutation`

## pattern (from lalph)

```typescript
// reactive issue fetching
export const currentIssuesAtom = Atom.family((projectId: ProjectId) =>
  pipe(
    issueSourceRuntime.atom(
      IssueSource.use((s) => s.issues(projectId))
    ),
    atomRuntime.withReactivity(["issues:" + projectId]),
    Atom.withRefresh("30 seconds"),
    Atom.keepAlive,
  ),
)

// mutations auto-invalidate
reactivity.mutation(
  { issues: [projectId] },
  impl.createIssue(projectId, issue),
)
```

## reference
- lalph: src/CurrentIssueSource.ts (currentIssuesAtom), src/IssueSource.ts (reactivity.mutation wrapper)
- lalph: src/Workers.ts (activeWorkersAtom, workerOutputAtom with Atom.family)
- repo: https://github.com/tim-smart/lalph

## verification
- `bun run typecheck` passes
- `bun run test` passes
- polling still works but is supplemented by reactive invalidation
- state changes propagate immediately on mutations

title: add ScopedRef for hot-swappable tracker client
description:
Wrap the tracker client in a `ScopedRef` so it can be transparently rebuilt when tokens expire or errors occur, without restarting the orchestrator.

## what changes
- packages/plot/src/tracker/: wrap tracker client creation in ScopedRef
- on IssueSourceError or auth errors, rebuild the client automatically
- add exponential backoff retry with `Schedule.exponential`

## pattern (from lalph)

```typescript
const build = Layer.build(source.layer).pipe(
  Effect.map(ServiceMap.get(IssueSource)),
)
const ref = yield* ScopedRef.fromAcquire(build)
const refresh = ScopedRef.set(ref, build)

// proxy methods that auto-refresh on error
issues: (projectId) =>
  ScopedRef.get(ref).pipe(
    Effect.flatMap((source) => source.issues(projectId)),
    Effect.tapErrorTag("IssueSourceError", () =>
      Effect.logWarning("Rebuilding...").pipe(
        Effect.andThen(Effect.ignore(refresh))
      )
    ),
    Effect.retry(refreshSchedule),
  ),
```

## reference
- lalph: src/CurrentIssueSource.ts
- repo: https://github.com/tim-smart/lalph

## verification
- `bun run typecheck` passes
- tracker client recovers from transient auth/network errors automatically

title: add stall detection (no-output timeout)
description:
Add stall detection that kills hung agents when they produce no output for a configurable duration. Currently plot only has a total turn timeout but no stall detection.

## what changes

### packages/plot/src/agent/
- wrap agent output stream with stall timeout
- if no output for `stall_timeout_ms` (from WORKFLOW.md config), kill the agent
- emit a `RunnerStalled` error that the orchestrator can handle

### packages/plot/src/core/
- orchestrator handles RunnerStalled: retry or decompose

## pattern (from lalph)

```typescript
// shared/stream.ts
export const withStallTimeout = (duration: Duration.Input) =>
  <A, E, R>(stream: Stream.Stream<A, E, R>) =>
    stream.pipe(
      Stream.timeoutFail({
        duration,
        onTimeout: () => new RunnerStalled(),
      }),
    )

// worker.ts
yield* handle.all.pipe(
  Stream.decodeText(),
  withStallTimeout(options.stallTimeout),
  Stream.runForEach(processChunk),
)
```

## config
Already have `stall_timeout_ms: 300000` in WORKFLOW.md — just need to enforce it.

## reference
- lalph: src/shared/stream.ts (withStallTimeout)
- lalph: src/Worktree.ts (execWithStallTimeout)
- lalph: src/commands/root.ts (stall-minutes flag)
- repo: https://github.com/tim-smart/lalph

## verification

- agents that hang are killed after stall timeout
- agents that produce output stay alive
